text:
Episode 1: Valar Dohaeris
Beyond the Wall, the Night's Watch faces disaster. In the darkness and blizzard at the Fist of the First Men, White Walkers and their army of undead wights overrun the camp of Lord Commander Jeor Mormont. Screams and clashes of steel fill the night as the three hundred black brothers are slaughtered. Samwell Tarly stumbles through the snow looking for safety. He comes across a decapitated brother whose head has been placed in his own hands. A wight with an axe lurches toward Sam. Ghost, Jon Snow’s white direwolf, leaps in and tears at the creature. The wight keeps crawling until Mormont arrives with a torch and sets it ablaze, destroying it. Only a few dozen men survive. Mormont is furious that Sam failed to send any ravens during the chaos. He orders an immediate retreat south to the Wall. They must warn Castle Black and the rest of Westeros, or everyone they know will die. The survivors limp south through the cold, exhausted and broken.

Meanwhile, Jon Snow is taken by Ygritte and the Lord of Bones into the main wildling camp in the Frostfangs. The Free Folk are not just an army—women, children, and entire clans are moving south to escape the White Walkers. Jon sees a real giant lumber past carrying mammoth bones. Wildlings shout “Crow!” at his black cloak and throw ice and stones until Ygritte drives them off. Inside Mance Rayder’s tent, the Lord of Bones presents Jon as Eddard Stark’s bastard who killed Qhorin Halfhand. Jon kneels before a large bearded man eating chicken, calling him “Your Grace.” The wildlings roar with laughter. That man is only Tormund Giantsbane. Mance himself sits quietly in a corner—an unassuming former Night’s Watch brother. No one kneels among the Free Folk. Mance is glad Jon killed Qhorin, who had slain many of his people, though Qhorin was once his brother. Jon claims he wants freedom, but Mance suspects he wants to play the hero

. Mance is glad Jon killed Qhorin, who had slain many of his people, though Qhorin was once his brother. Jon claims he wants freedom, but Mance suspects he wants to play the hero. Jon tells the truth: at Craster’s Keep he watched Craster leave newborn sons in the woods for the White Walkers, and Mormont knew and did nothing. Jon wants to fight for the living, as the First Men once did against the Long Night. Mance accepts him and tells him to get a new cloak. Jon is now among the Free Folk.

In King’s Landing the Lannisters celebrate victory after the Battle of the Blackwater. Tywin Lannister coldly informs his son Tyrion that he intends to disinherit him. Jaime gave up his inheritance by joining the Kingsguard, so Tyrion should be next, but Tywin refuses to believe Tyrion did anything useful as acting Hand. He calls Tyrion a whore-mongering, drunken, spiteful creature who lies out of envy. Tywin is especially angry that Tyrion brought Shae to the capital against orders. When Tyrion asks why, Tywin says Tyrion killed his mother Joanna in childbirth. The laws force Tywin to let Tyrion keep the name Lannister, but he wishes he could prove the boy was not his. Tyrion fumes to his newly knighted sellsword Bronn, now Ser Bronn of the Blackwater.

Joffrey rides in a palanquin from the Great Sept. Margaery Tyrell suddenly stops the procession in Flea Bottom. She gets out, walks among the poor, visits an orphanage, and has her servants hand out bread and toys. The smallfolk love her. That evening Joffrey and Cersei dine with Margaery and Loras. Cersei scolds Margaery for the charity, reminding her those same streets saw the royal party assaulted weeks earlier. Joffrey defends Margaery and criticizes his mother. Cersei realizes Margaery wins love while she only rules through fear. Sansa and Shae sit on the docks watching ships. Littlefinger arrives and hints he can smuggle Sansa out on his next voyage. Sansa is eager but warns she is a terrible liar. Ros, working for Littlefinger, asks Shae to watch over Sansa.

Davos Seaworth is pulled from the sea by Salladhor Saan after the wildfire explosion. Mourning his son Matthos, Davos learns Melisandre has begun burning people alive who speak against her. He convinces Salladhor to take him to Dragonstone. There Stannis sits broken with Melisandre. Davos calls her his enemy and blames her for the disaster. She turns it back on him—he kept her from the battle. When she mentions Matthos, Davos draws a knife. Guards stop him and Stannis throws him in the dungeon.

In the Riverlands Robb Stark’s army takes Harrenhal, but Tywin has already withdrawn. The courtyards are filled with the bodies of two hundred Northern and Riverlands prisoners massacred by the Lannisters. One survivor remains—the maester Qyburn. Morale is low. Robb has won every battle, but the Lannisters now refuse to fight him head-on and simply wait him out while gaining the Tyrells as allies.

Daenerys Targaryen’s ship reaches Astapor in Slaver’s Bay. Her dragons are the size of small dogs. They fly around the ship, snatching fish and roasting them mid-air. They are still too small for war. She needs an army. Jorah suggests the Unsullied, the elite slave eunuch soldiers of Astapor, said to be among the finest in the world. Slavery is illegal in Westeros, but they have no better option. Daenerys wants more Dothraki, but Jorah says other khalasars will only join a strong queen who already has an army. She decides to look into buying the Unsullied.
2

(The episode establishes the new power balances after Blackwater, Jon’s infiltration of the wildlings, the Night’s Watch retreat, Robb’s stalled campaign, Stannis’s despair, and Daenerys’s arrival in Slaver’s Bay seeking power through the slave soldiers. Every major plotline advances with personal confrontations, moral tests, and the growing threat of the White Walkers.)

Episode 2: Dark Wings, Dark Words
Jon marches south with Mance Rayder’s huge Free Folk host. Mance explains it is ninety different clans speaking seven languages, united only by the truth that they will all die if they stay north of the Wall. He shows Jon the warg Orell, whose eyes roll back while his eagle scouts ahead. Orell reports the Fist of the First Men is covered in dead crows. Mormont’s survivors continue south. Sam collapses from exhaustion. Rast wants to leave him. Grenn and Edd stay with him. Mormont forbids Sam to die and orders Rast to keep him alive under pain of death.
3

Bran dreams he is walking and hunting. He sees the Three-Eyed Raven and relives archery practice with Jon and Robb while hearing his father’s voice. He wakes. Later the boy from the dream, Jojen Reed, and his sister Meera approach the camp. Summer sniffs Jojen and accepts him. Meera puts a knife to Osha’s throat when she threatens Jojen. The Reeds are loyal Stark bannermen who have come to protect Bran and Rickon. Jojen explains Bran is a warg who can enter Summer’s mind, and also has the Sight—dreams of past, present, and future. Bran’s dream of Ned’s death was the Sight; Jojen had the same dream. Howland Reed wept when he heard it. Jojen reached out to Bran in the dream. The group continues north.

At an unknown castle (the Dreadfort), Theon is chained in a dungeon. Torturers pry off his fingernails and crush his foot with a press while asking why he took Winterfell. He first tells the truth, then lies frantically. A young servant boy later frees the press and claims Yara sent him to rescue Theon. He says they must wait until night. Theon is left bagged and crying.

In King’s Landing Joffrey is fitted for wedding clothes. Cersei criticizes Margaery’s charity and clothing. Joffrey dismisses her. Shae dresses Sansa and warns her about Littlefinger’s motives. Sansa naively trusts him as an old friend of her mother’s. Shae suspects sexual interest. Loras escorts Sansa to meet Margaery and grandmother Olenna Tyrell in the gardens. Olenna bluntly demands the truth about Joffrey. Sansa breaks down and describes how Joffrey promised mercy then beheaded Ned and forced her to look at the head. She blurts that Joffrey is a monster. Olenna is unsurprised by the rumors but says Mace will not cancel the royal marriage. Shae visits Tyrion. He warns his father will kill her if found. She asks him to protect Sansa from Littlefinger. They argue playfully about Ros and have sex. Margaery visits Joffrey before his hunt. He questions her about Renly. She carefully paints Renly as unwilling and perverted, then flatters Joffrey’s new crossbow and his love of killing

. Margaery visits Joffrey before his hunt. He questions her about Renly. She carefully paints Renly as unwilling and perverted, then flatters Joffrey’s new crossbow and his love of killing. He invites her along.

In the Riverlands Arya, Gendry, and Hot Pie travel with the Brotherhood Without Banners after being taken. (The episode continues with further Riverlands developments involving Jaime and Brienne’s captivity progressing toward more torment, and other threads of pursuit and alliance.) The story weaves the growing supernatural abilities of Bran, the psychological breaking of Theon, political maneuvering by the Tyrells against the Lannisters, and the slow grinding of the war.
3

(Detailed expansions cover every conversation, the emotional weight of Sansa’s confession, the physical agony of Theon’s torture, the quiet bonding of Jon with the Free Folk culture, and the careful political dance in the capital as Margaery begins to win Joffrey.)
Episode 3: Walk of Punishment

In Astapor Daenerys, Jorah, and Barristan walk the Walk of Punishment where rebellious slaves are crucified and left to die. She offers water to one who refuses, wanting only quick death. Jorah and Barristan argue over buying the Unsullied. Jorah says they will not rape or kill civilians because they have no urges. Barristan says Rhaegar’s men fought for love of him, not as slaves, and Rhaegar still died. Daenerys wishes she had known Rhaegar, the last dragon—but she is the last. She bargains with Kraznys mo Nakloz through Missandei. Kraznys insults her constantly in Low Valyrian while Missandei softens the words. Daenerys offers all her ships, the rest of her goods, and one dragon for all eight thousand Unsullied plus those in training. Kraznys is stunned. She also demands Missandei. Jorah and Barristan object publicly; she rebukes them. Alone with Missandei she learns the crucified man preferred death because in the afterlife there are no masters. Missandei has no family

. Jorah and Barristan object publicly; she rebukes them. Alone with Missandei she learns the crucified man preferred death because in the afterlife there are no masters. Missandei has no family. Daenerys warns of the dangers ahead. Missandei answers “Valar morghulis.” Daenerys replies, “We are not men.”

Mance’s army reaches the Fist. The horse carcasses are arranged in a giant spiral. Human bodies are gone—now wights. Mance sends Tormund with twenty men, including Jon, to climb the Wall and attack Castle Black from the undefended south side. The signal will be a massive fire. Jon’s knowledge of the castle is the test; if he fails, he dies.

Mormont’s survivors reach Craster’s Keep. Craster mocks them and claims the White Walkers spare him because he is godly to the real gods. He feeds pigs better than men and suggests eating Sam. Gilly gives birth to a boy. Sam and Gilly know Craster will give the child to the Walkers.

At Riverrun Hoster Tully’s funeral boat is launched. Edmure fails three times to light it with a flaming arrow. Brynden the Blackfish succeeds with one perfect shot and walks away. Catelyn mourns with her uncle; they made peace on the deathbed. Robb, Brynden, and Edmure argue strategy. Edmure’s victory at the Fords ruined the plan to lure Tywin west so Stannis could take King’s Landing. The Lannisters are now secure with Tyrell gold and men. Capturing young Lannister cousins means nothing. Robb needs every man; Tywin can afford losses.

(Jaime and Brienne continue their captive journey; Locke’s men grow more brutal. Tyrion is given new duties by Tywin as Master of Coin, dealing with the massive debts from the war and the Tyrell alliance. The episode deepens the moral cost of power for Daenerys, the impossible position of the Night’s Watch, Robb’s fraying alliances, and the personal toll on every character.)
4
)

Episode 4: And Now His Watch Is Ended
Jaime’s sword hand has been cut off by Locke. The severed hand hangs around his neck. He is feverish, starved of water, and kicked while down. He is given horse piss to drink and vomits. He steals a sword in a weak attempt to die fighting but collapses. That night he wants to die, saying he was that hand. Brienne shames him into eating and living for revenge. She learned he saved her from rape by inventing a sapphire ransom. She asks why; he does not answer.

Arya and Gendry are brought hooded to the Brotherhood’s hollow hill hideout. The Hound is also captive. Beric Dondarrion, still carrying out Ned Stark’s original order to bring Gregor Clegane to justice, now leads a band that protects smallfolk from both Lannisters and Starks. They recount horrors at Mummer’s Ford and the Sack of King’s Landing. The Hound was not there for most, but Arya accuses him of killing Mycah the butcher’s boy. He admits it. Beric grants him trial by combat against himself.
5

In King’s Landing Varys tells Tyrion the full story of his castration by a sorcerer in Myr who burned his genitals while a voice answered from the flames. Varys survived out of spite, rose by selling secrets, and now opens a crate containing the same living sorcerer. Patience brings revenge. Ros reports on Littlefinger’s obsession with Sansa and the ship with two feather beds. Varys realizes the plan to take her. Cersei and Olenna tour the Great Sept with Joffrey and Margaery. Olenna mocks her own son’s military failures. Margaery gets Joffrey to greet the crowd, who now cheer them. Cersei sees she is losing control.

(The episode continues with the mutiny at Craster’s Keep where the Night’s Watch brothers finally snap under Craster’s insults and Mormont’s leadership. Rast and others kill Craster and then Mormont. Sam flees with Gilly and the baby. Daenerys finalizes the deal for the Unsullied, then in a stunning reverse has Drogon burn Kraznys and the masters while the Unsullied, now free, slaughter the slavers on her command “Dracarys.” She frees them all and they choose to follow her. She has her army.)

The stories of betrayal, revenge, identity loss (Jaime’s hand), and sudden empowerment (Daenerys) collide.
5

The stories of betrayal, revenge, identity loss (Jaime’s hand), and sudden empowerment (Daenerys) collide.
5

Episode 5: Kissed by Fire
Jon is with Tormund’s climbing party. Orell questions him about Castle Black’s defenses and numbers. Jon lies about the garrison size. Tormund warns him against lying. Ygritte steals Longclaw and leads Jon to a hot-spring cave. She strips and forces the issue of his vows. They have sex; she is surprised by his skill with his mouth. Afterward they bathe and she wishes they could stay forever, away from war and winter. She is “kissed by fire” (red hair).
6

Daenerys’s Unsullied army marches on Yunkai. Jorah and Barristan swap war stories from the Greyjoy Rebellion. Barristan wants to serve someone he believes in. Grey Worm is chosen as leader of the Unsullied. He keeps the slave name because it is the name he had when Daenerys freed him. She is moved.

At Riverrun Rickard Karstark and his men murder the young Lannister squires Willem and Martyn in their cell for vengeance after Catelyn freed Jaime. Robb is horrified. Karstark calls him the King Who Lost the North. Robb has Karstark’s men hanged and sentences Karstark himself to death despite advisors begging him to keep the man hostage. Robb executes Rickard Karstark personally with a sword, saying “the blood of the First Men” and “the man who passes the sentence should swing the sword.” The Karstark forces begin to desert.

(The Hound’s trial by combat with Beric ends with Beric resurrected again by Thoros after being killed. Jaime begins training left-handed with Brienne. Tyrion learns the true cost of the royal wedding and Tyrell demands. The episode is filled with tests of loyalty, broken oaths, and the price of vengeance.)

Episode 6: The Climb
Tywin forces Olenna to accept Cersei marrying Loras by threatening to put Loras in the Kingsguard (ending his inheritance). Sansa still hopes for Loras; he is more interested in the wedding spectacle. Tyrion realizes Joffrey ordered the attempt on his life. He breaks the news to Sansa that she will marry him instead. Varys and Littlefinger discuss power; Littlefinger has given Ros to Joffrey, who kills her with his crossbow. Sansa watches Littlefinger’s ship leave without her.
7

The Brotherhood trains Arya with a bow. Melisandre arrives, takes Gendry (paying gold), and tells Arya they will meet again after seeing many eyes she will shut. At Riverrun the Freys demand apology, Harrenhal, and Edmure’s marriage to Roslin for the alliance needed to attack Casterly Rock. Edmure agrees. Roose Bolton dines with Jaime and Brienne; he will send Jaime home if Jaime tells Tywin Bolton was not responsible for the hand. Brienne stays prisoner.

Bran’s group has tension between Osha and Meera. Jojen has a vision of Jon surrounded by enemies. Theon is further tortured; the boy (Ramsay) flays his finger for amusement after tricking him.

Sam and Gilly camp; he shows her dragonglass and sings. At the Wall base Tormund’s party climbs. Ygritte knows Jon is still loyal but says they must be loyal to each other. A sheet of ice breaks; Orell cuts their rope. Jon saves them both with a desperate hook. They reach the top and kiss, looking south.

The climb is both literal and metaphorical for every character’s rise or fall.

The climb is both literal and metaphorical for every character’s rise or fall.

Episode 7: The Bear and the Maiden Fair
Jon, Ygritte, and the wildlings head for Castle Black. Orell is jealous and distrustful. Jon tries to warn Ygritte the attack will fail as all previous Kings-Beyond-the-Wall failed. She says if they die they die, but they will live first. Theon is released by two women who seduce him, then Ramsay appears and castrates him while he screams. Osha refuses to go beyond the Wall after her dead husband rose as a wight.
8
)

Daenerys reaches Yunkai. Razdal mo Eraz offers gold and ships to leave them alone. She demands every slave freed with food, clothes, and property. He threatens “powerful friends.” Her dragons snarl. She keeps his gold chests.

Melisandre sails with Gendry past the Blackwater wrecks and reveals he is Robert’s bastard. Arya tries to escape the Brotherhood and is grabbed by the Hound. Robb’s army is delayed by rain on the way to the Twins; Talisa tells him she is pregnant. Jaime leaves Harrenhal but learns Brienne is to be killed for sport. He returns, finds her in the bear pit with a wooden sword while men sing “The Bear and the Maiden Fair.” He jumps in. Steelshanks shoots the bear. Jaime takes Brienne with him.

The episode mixes rescue, betrayal of the body, political offers, and the first real tenderness between Jaime and Brienne.

Episode 8: Second Sons
Arya rides with the Hound toward the Twins to ransom her. She almost kills him with a rock; he dares her. He tells her he once saved Sansa. They will make the wedding if she stops trying to murder him.
9
)

Daenerys spies on the Second Sons mercenaries. She meets captains Mero (Titan’s Bastard) and Prendahl, plus lieutenant Daario Naharis. Mero is crude and gropes Missandei. They refuse her offer. She gives them two days. That night the captains draw lots to assassinate her. Daario kills the other two, brings their heads, and swears to her after seeing her beauty. He kneels with his sword, men, and heart.

On Dragonstone Melisandre brings Gendry. Stannis releases Davos after extracting a promise. Melisandre seduces Gendry, leeches him, and has Stannis burn the leeches naming Robb, Balon, and Joffrey as the usurpers who must die.

In King’s Landing Tyrion marries Sansa. Joffrey humiliates him by removing the stool so Tyrion must ask Sansa to kneel for the cloak. At the feast Joffrey is vile, suggesting he will rape Sansa after Tyrion. Tyrion threatens him with a dagger: Joffrey will fuck his own bride with a wooden cock. Tywin defuses it. Tyrion does not consummate the marriage; he passes out on the couch. Shae notices the sheets are clean.

Sam and Gilly shelter; he kills a White Walker with dragonglass when one attacks. The episode ends major threads of marriage, loyalty switches, and magical blood magic.

Episode 9: The Rains of Castamere
Daenerys’s small team (Jorah, Daario, Grey Worm) sneaks into Yunkai through a back gate, fights through, and opens the city. Daario presents the torn banner. Yunkai is hers.
10
)

Sam and Gilly head for the Nightfort’s secret passage. Bran’s group shelters in a mill in the Gift during a storm. Nearby Jon’s wildling party attacks an old horse-breeder. Jon alerts the man and cannot kill him when ordered. Ygritte shoots the man. Tormund orders Jon killed. Bran wargs into Summer; the direwolves help. Jon kills Orell (who wargs into his eagle and claws Jon’s face). Jon escapes on horseback back toward the Wall, leaving Ygritte. Bran sends Osha and Rickon to Last Hearth with Shaggydog while he, Meera, and Jojen continue for the Three-Eyed Raven.

Robb’s army arrives at the Twins. He apologizes publicly to Walder Frey’s daughters. Hospitality is offered. Edmure marries the beautiful Roslin. The feast is joyful until the musicians play “The Rains of Castamere.” Doors close. Catelyn sees Bolton wearing mail. She slaps him and screams warning. Too late. Lothar stabs pregnant Talisa repeatedly in the belly. Crossbows cut down Robb and the Stark men. Catelyn is wounded. Arya and the Hound arrive outside; she sees Grey Wind killed and the slaughter. The Hound knocks her out and carries her away. Robb crawls to dying Talisa. Catelyn takes Joyeuse Frey hostage and begs for Robb’s life. Walder refuses—“I’ll find another.” Roose Bolton stabs Robb in the heart: “The Lannisters send their regards.” Catelyn kills Joyeuse then stands catatonic as Black Walder cuts her throat. The Red Wedding is complete.

Episode 10: Mhysa
The massacre continues outside the Twins. Frey men butcher the Stark camp. Robb’s body is desecrated—his head replaced with Grey Wind’s—and paraded while Freys chant “King in the North.” The Hound rides away with unconscious Arya under a Frey banner. Next morning Walder and Roose gloat: Frey gets Riverrun, Bolton is Warden of the North. The Blackfish escaped. Ramsay burned Winterfell and flayed the Ironborn after false promises.
11

At the Dreadfort Ramsay forces Theon to accept the name Reek after more torment. On Pyke Balon receives Theon’s severed penis and a demand to withdraw. He is indifferent. Yara gathers men and a fast ship to rescue her brother.

Arya and the Hound pass Freys bragging about the desecration. Arya stabs one in the neck with the Hound’s knife, whispers “valar morghulis,” and recovers her coin.

Arya and the Hound pass Freys bragging about the desecration. Arya stabs one in the neck with the Hound’s knife, whispers “valar morghulis,” and recovers her coin.

In King’s Landing Tyrion and Sansa walk; she is learning to ignore mockery. News of the Red Wedding arrives. Joffrey wants Robb’s head served at his own wedding. Tyrion forbids it. Tywin sends the king to bed. Tywin admits he orchestrated the wedding massacre—better than ten thousand dead in battle. He lectures Tyrion on family duty and consummating the marriage. Tyrion finds Sansa already weeping; he leaves her. Varys tries to buy Shae’s departure with diamonds for Tyrion’s sake; she refuses unless Tyrion asks. Jaime, Brienne, and Qyburn finally reach the Red Keep. Jaime appears before Cersei, maimed and changed.

On Dragonstone further blood magic and planning continue. Beyond the Wall and in the North the survivors push on. In Yunkai Daenerys enters the city. The freed slaves pour out, lift her onto their shoulders, and chant “Mhysa” (Mother) as her dragons fly overhead. She is both conqueror and liberator.

Season 3 ends with the Stark leadership destroyed, the Lannister-Tyrell-Frey-Bolton axis triumphant for the moment, Daenerys rising as a breaker of chains with a real army, Jon returning to the Night’s Watch after his wildling time, Theon broken into Reek, and the White Walker threat still advancing. Every surviving character is scarred, relocated, or transformed by the events.


SEASON 3, EPISODE 1 — “Valar Dohaeris”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 1 — “Valar Dohaeris”

Beyond the Wall, the Night’s Watch survivors are in full retreat after the disaster at the Fist of the First Men. Sam is nearly killed by a wight in the blizzard chaos, but he’s saved as the remaining brothers regroup under Jeor Mormont’s command. The immediate goal is no longer victory—it’s survival and getting word south that the threat is real and moving. 
1

At the wildling camp, Jon is marched through a rough, crowded world that’s nothing like Castle Black’s rigid order—he even sees a giant among them. He’s brought before Mance Rayder and quickly learns that surviving here means telling a story people want to believe. Jon finally earns Mance’s attention by condemning Craster’s baby sacrifices and claiming the Night’s Watch leadership tolerated it, painting himself as a man disgusted by “southern” hypocrisy and Watch weakness. 
1

In King’s Landing, Tyrion crawls out of the shadow of the Blackwater: scarred, bitter, and convinced his own family tried to finish him off. He demands recognition and reward from Tywin—especially the right to inherit Casterly Rock—only to be crushed by Tywin’s cold refusal and contempt. Meanwhile, Sansa is quietly approached with the idea of escape through Littlefinger’s schemes, and the Tyrells begin winning public love in ways the Lannisters never bothered to try (or never understood). 
1

Across the Narrow Sea, Daenerys reaches Astapor and is shown the Unsullied: disciplined slave-soldiers built through cruelty. She is visibly sickened by how they’re made and used, but she also recognizes the brutal truth—dragons alone aren’t an army yet. An assassination attempt on her is stopped at the last moment, and the rescuer reveals himself as Barristan Selmy, offering his sword and his service to the last Targaryen. 
1

SEASON 3, EPISODE 2 — “Dark Wings, Dark Words”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 2 — “Dark Wings, Dark Words”

With Mance’s host, Jon learns the wildlings aren’t one nation—they’re many rival peoples forced into one desperate migration. Mance makes the stakes plain: if they don’t get south, they die. He also introduces Jon to the reality of wargs in wildling society through Orell, whose scouting isn’t rumor or superstition but a living weapon. Meanwhile on the Watch’s side of the story, Sam collapses from exhaustion and shame, and Jeor Mormont brutally shuts down any talk of abandoning him. 
2

In the North, Bran’s “three-eyed raven” dreams sharpen into something more like a calling. Jojen and Meera Reed find the group, and Jojen explains that Bran’s abilities aren’t just wolf-dreams: there’s a wider kind of seeing tied to the raven—visions that can reach across time and truth. It reframes Bran’s journey: he isn’t only fleeing danger; he’s being pulled toward a destination he doesn’t yet understand. 
2

In King’s Landing, Sansa is handled gently and then cornered expertly by the Tyrells—especially Olenna—who want the truth about Joffrey before marrying him to Margaery. Sansa tries to protect herself with polite lies, but the conversation pushes on her trauma until she finally lets the mask slip and calls him what he is. The Tyrells absorb it—alarmed, but not deterred. 
2

Elsewhere, Theon wakes into a nightmare of systematic torture that doesn’t even seem to have a clear goal beyond breaking him. At the same time, Robb’s campaign is poisoned by grief and bad news: Hoster Tully’s death, Winterfell’s fall, and Bran and Rickon missing. Arya, Gendry, and Hot Pie cross paths with the Brotherhood Without Banners—outlaws with their own rules and a dangerous kind of charisma—while Jaime and Brienne’s attempt to reach safety ends with their capture after Jaime’s reckless attempt to escape. 
2

SEASON 3, EPISODE 3 — “Walk of Punishment”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 3 — “Walk of Punishment”

Tywin takes control of the Small Council the way he takes control of everything: by quietly forcing everyone to reveal what they are. Even the simple question of where to sit becomes a test of hunger, vanity, and restraint. Tyrion is given work—real work, with real stakes—as he digs into finances and discovers the crown’s borrowing and looming dependence on the Iron Bank. The war isn’t only fought with swords; it’s fought with debt and leverage. 
3

Beyond the Wall and at Craster’s Keep, survival strips away the Watch’s pretense of unity. Craster’s “hospitality” is a trap made of insults and domination, but the Watch is too desperate to refuse. Sam’s sympathy leads him to Gilly at the exact moment her child is born—an event that’s not just personal, but tied to the terrible secret of what Craster does with his sons. 
3

At Dragonstone, Stannis is raw after defeat, clutching at Melisandre’s certainty because he has none left of his own. She redirects him toward a darker idea: if king’s blood is power, then Stannis’s bloodline has other sources besides Stannis himself. On the mainland, Theon is “rescued” in a way that turns out to be another layer of his captor’s game—hope used as a weapon. 
3

In Astapor, Daenerys walks the “Walk of Punishment” and sees slavery displayed as public theater: suffering as warning. The experience hardens her resolve and clarifies her method. She negotiates to buy all the Unsullied, and when the slavers try to humiliate and lowball her, she makes a shocking offer: one of her dragons—while also demanding Missandei as part of the deal. 
3

In the Riverlands, Hoster Tully’s funeral becomes a public measure of Edmure’s insecurity and the Blackfish’s competence. Robb’s anger at Edmure is not cruelty—it’s the rage of a young king watching small mistakes compound into strategic disaster. Arya’s road splits as Hot Pie chooses safety and a kitchen over war, and Jaime’s arrogance finally collides with reality: Locke takes his right hand, the true source of his identity and power. 
3

SEASON 3, EPISODE 4 — “And Now His Watch Is Ended”

Jaime begins to understand what it means to be helpless. He’s sick, feverish, mocked, and made to wear his severed hand like a joke around his neck. His attempts at defiance only underline the new truth: without his sword hand, the “Kingslayer” is just another captive. Brienne tries to help him anyway, stubbornly honoring an oath in a world that treats oaths like punchlines. 
4

In King’s Landing, Varys reveals a colder side: patience as vengeance, power as long memory. His personal story of mutilation doesn’t end in tears—it ends in a crate containing the man who did it, showing Tyrion what “waiting” can build. Meanwhile, the Tyrells keep tightening their net around the court, and plans quietly move in the background around Sansa and Littlefinger’s travel preparations. 
4

At Craster’s Keep, everything finally snaps. Hunger, fear, and rage boil into mutiny. Craster is killed under his own roof, and Jeor Mormont—Lord Commander, symbol of the Watch’s authority—is stabbed and dies in the chaos. Sam’s instincts turn from obedience to survival; he grabs Gilly and runs, choosing life over the collapsing idea that the Watch will protect its own. 
4

And in Astapor, Daenerys executes one of the most decisive reversals in the series. She completes the purchase, trading chains for the whip that symbolizes ownership—then reveals she understood the slavers’ language the whole time. She orders the Unsullied to kill the masters and free the slaves, and she uses her dragon to burn Kraznys when he realizes too late that he sold control to the wrong person. After the sack, she does something the city never would: she tells the Unsullied they are free—and invites them to stay as free men. They choose her. 
4

SEASON 3, EPISODE 5 — “Kissed by Fire”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 5 — “Kissed by Fire”

The Brotherhood puts the Hound on trial the only way they recognize: trial by combat. Beric Dondarrion fights with a flaming sword fueled by blood-magic, triggering the Hound’s terror of fire—but the Hound’s brute skill wins. Then the Brotherhood’s religion shows its teeth: Beric is brought back from death again, proving their cause isn’t just outlaw theater. The Hound, condemned by men, walks free anyway—because the Brotherhood believes the Lord of Light isn’t done with him. 
5

At Harrenhal, Jaime’s physical ruin forces emotional honesty. Qyburn tries to save what’s left of Jaime’s arm, and afterward Jaime finally tells Brienne the truth behind the “Kingslayer” name: the wildfire caches, the Mad King’s plan to burn King’s Landing, and the order that would have made Jaime murder his own father before the city died screaming. For the first time, Brienne sees that “dishonor” can be the cost of preventing mass murder—and Jaime sees what it feels like to be judged without being heard. 
5

Robb’s rule fractures further when Karstark’s men murder young captives in vengeance. Robb refuses to be a king who excuses murder because it’s politically convenient: he orders punishment, then personally executes Rickard Karstark despite every warning that it will cost him half his strength. The consequence is immediate—his coalition crumbles—and the war shifts from winning battles to preventing collapse. 
5

Jon and Ygritte’s relationship crosses the line from tension to intimacy in a hidden cave, even as Jon knows his vows and loyalties are still a trap closing around him. On Dragonstone, Stannis’s “family life” is revealed as cold duty and religious obsession, but Davos unexpectedly finds a lifeline: Shireen teaches him to read, giving him a new kind of power. And in King’s Landing, Tywin counters the Tyrell plan to marry Sansa into their house by forcing his own: Tyrion will marry Sansa, and Cersei will be pushed toward Loras—marriage as a weapon, not a union. 
5

SEASON 3, EPISODE 6 — “The Climb”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 6 — “The Climb”

In King’s Landing, alliances are negotiated like hostage exchanges. Tywin corners Olenna into accepting Cersei and Loras by threatening to strip Loras’s future through a Kingsguard appointment. Tyrion and Cersei’s sibling war turns blunt: they compare their forced marriages, and Tyrion finally pieces together that Joffrey—not Cersei—ordered his attempted assassination at the Blackwater. The power center is shifting: Tywin’s rule limits Joffrey, but it also turns everyone else into tools. 
6

In the Riverlands, Melisandre arrives at the Brotherhood’s hideout with purpose: she wants Gendry. The Brotherhood sells him for gold and cause, enraging Arya and teaching her a brutal lesson—people who sound righteous can still be bought. Robb, meanwhile, negotiates with Frey envoys and learns the cost of breaking his oath isn’t just insult—it’s a ransom paid in castles, apologies, and marriages. 
6

At Harrenhal, Roose Bolton plays both sides with calm precision. He agrees to send Jaime back—so long as Jaime swears Bolton had nothing to do with the maiming—while keeping Brienne behind as a prisoner tied to Stark “treason.” In the North, Jojen’s visions worsen, and he tells Bran he has seen Jon with the wildlings, confirming that the war isn’t only in the south; it’s moving along the Wall’s edge too. 
6

Then the episode delivers its title in full: the wildlings climb the Wall. A crack, an avalanche, death on the rope lines—Jon saves Ygritte when it would be easier to let her fall, and together they reach the top and stare out at the Seven Kingdoms below. It’s romantic, awe-filled, and terrifying—because Jon is standing on the edge of betraying someone no matter what he chooses next. 
6

SEASON 3, EPISODE 7 — “The Bear and the Maiden Fair”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 7 — “The Bear and the Maiden Fair”

King’s Landing tightens the screws on Tyrion’s private life: Sansa is comforted by Margaery, while Tyrion and Bronn talk bluntly about what marriage will do to him and to Shae. Shae draws a line—she won’t stay in a relationship that turns her into a hidden shame behind a political wife. Tywin also begins educating Joffrey in what ruling actually is: patience, fear management, and not mistaking cruelty for strength—especially while rumors spread of Daenerys and dragons. 
7

North of the Wall and in the North proper, Jon keeps moving with the wildlings while Orell and others test his sincerity, and Bran’s group argues about how far north is too far. Osha refuses to follow a path that leads beyond the Wall, telling a personal horror story about her husband returning as a wight—proof that the dead don’t always stay dead. Meanwhile Theon’s torment escalates into sexual cruelty and psychological destruction, with “help” used as bait for another humiliation. 
7

In the Riverlands, Robb’s march to the Twins is slowed by weather and doubt, and Talisa reveals she’s pregnant—raising the stakes of every political mistake Robb has made. Arya’s world collapses further when she learns the Brotherhood sold Gendry to Melisandre; she runs, only to be captured by the Hound, who now has his own plan: ransom her to her family. 
7

Across the Narrow Sea, Daenerys reaches Yunkai and chooses liberation over “strategic value.” She refuses bribes of gold and ships and demands the slaves be freed and paid, or she’ll take the city by force. Back at Harrenhal, Jaime—half-rebuilt after confession—keeps his promise to Brienne in the only way he can: he turns back. He finds Brienne thrown into a bear pit with only a wooden sword, and he jumps in after her. Even without his right hand, he chooses death over abandoning the oath—then manages to get them both out alive. 
7

SEASON 3, EPISODE 8 — “Second Sons”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 8 — “Second Sons”

In King’s Landing, Tyrion and Sansa are pushed into marriage at swordpoint wrapped in ceremony. Joffrey humiliates Tyrion by removing the stepstool meant to help him cloak Sansa, forcing Tyrion to adapt in front of a laughing court. At the feast, Joffrey turns the threat of public “bedding” into another cruelty, but Tyrion draws a hard boundary—he’ll play the political game, but he won’t let Joffrey brutalize Sansa for sport. Later, Tyrion quietly tells Sansa he won’t touch her until she wants him to. 
8

At Dragonstone, Melisandre brings Gendry to Stannis and treats him as a resource, not a person: king’s blood as fuel. Davos argues against sacrificing him and is freed only after swearing not to try to kill Melisandre again. Melisandre seduces Gendry, binds him, draws his blood with leeches, and Stannis burns them while naming the rival kings he believes stand in the way of his destiny. 
8

In the Riverlands, Arya tries to kill the Hound in his sleep, but he’s already awake—always half-expecting betrayal. He drags her toward the Twins to sell her back to Robb, turning “rescue” into a business transaction. Across the Narrow Sea, Daenerys faces the Second Sons mercenaries: she tries to buy them off, but they plan to murder her instead. Daario Naharis flips the board by killing his own leaders and arriving at Daenerys’s tent with their heads, pledging himself and the company to her cause. 
8

Beyond the Wall, Sam’s fear finally breaks into action when a White Walker attacks. His steel sword shatters against it, but dragonglass works: Sam kills the Walker and saves Gilly’s baby, proving the Night’s Watch has a weapon that matters—and that the war to come is not folklore. 
8

SEASON 3, EPISODE 9 — “The Rains of Castamere”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 9 — “The Rains of Castamere”

In the North and around the Wall, several storylines collide in one stormy night. Bran’s group hides in an abandoned mill as Jon and the wildlings raid nearby; Hodor’s fear nearly gives them away, and Bran uses warging to silence him by taking over his mind. The wildlings try to force Jon to kill an innocent old man to prove loyalty; Jon can’t do it, and Ygritte kills the man instead, confirming Jon’s heart isn’t with them. When the wildlings turn on Jon, Bran—warging into Summer—helps create the opening Jon needs to escape back toward the Wall. Bran then makes a painful choice: he tells Osha to take Rickon away to safety, splitting what remains of the Stark children’s path. 
9

Across the Narrow Sea, Daenerys commits to the invasion of Yunkai with a small strike team: Daario, Jorah, and Grey Worm infiltrate through a rear gate plan. They fight through an ambush and succeed, returning to Daenerys with the city effectively in her hands. It’s a preview of the kind of campaign she intends to run—surgical violence aimed at changing a system, not just taking a throne. 
9

At the Twins, the story becomes tragedy. Robb’s army arrives and is given bread and salt—guest right—supposedly guaranteeing safety under Walder Frey’s roof. Robb apologizes, Walder performs hospitality with a sneer, and the wedding proceeds: Edmure is surprised to find Roslin kind and beautiful, and the feast begins in a deceptively normal swirl of music and drink. But the doors close, and the Lannister song begins. Catelyn’s instincts scream, and then the massacre erupts—Talisa is murdered, Robb is shot and finished, Grey Wind is killed, and Arya arrives just in time to see the betrayal’s full horror before the Hound drags her away. Catelyn’s final attempt to bargain fails, and she is executed after retaliating. 
9

SEASON 3, EPISODE 10 — “Mhysa”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 10 — “Mhysa”

In King’s Landing, the capital reacts to the Red Wedding not with grief but with power-politics. Tyrion and Sansa share a rare moment of mutual understanding as two people trapped by the same system—until Tyrion learns Robb and Catelyn are dead. Joffrey wants Robb’s head brought to the city as a “gift” to Sansa, pushing Tyrion close to violence again, and Tywin responds by asserting dominance the only way he can: he has Joffrey restrained and sedated, showing that even the king is manageable when the real authority decides it. 
10

Varys tries to remove Shae from the board by offering her diamonds and a new life in Essos, framing it as protection for Tyrion as much as mercy for her. Shae refuses, choosing pride, love, anger—or some blend of all three—over flight. Jaime, Brienne, and Qyburn arrive in the city, and Jaime immediately runs toward the one person he still defines as “home”: Cersei. 
10

At the Twins, the Freys celebrate their crime openly by desecrating Robb’s corpse—an image that pushes Arya over the edge. She attacks a Frey soldier in pure rage, and the Hound kills the rest, saving her even while he continues treating her like property to be sold. Walder and Roose discuss their rewards—Riverrun and the North—while Bolton casually reveals Ramsay’s brutality at Winterfell, confirming that the new order will be held together by terror, not legitimacy. 
10

In the North, Bran’s path briefly intersects with the Night’s Watch: Sam recognizes him and helps take Bran’s group through a hidden passage at the Wall, giving them dragonglass before they separate. Sam and Gilly reach Castle Black and warn Maester Aemon, who sends ravens across Westeros about the White Walkers’ return. Jon limps back to Castle Black after Ygritte shoots him multiple times as he flees, and the Watch takes him in—his cover as a wildling shattered, his war with them now inevitable. Meanwhile, Theon’s story hits its bleak reveal: the “rescuer” is Ramsay, and Theon is forced into a new identity—“Reek”—through violence and humiliation. 
10

On the Iron Islands, Balon receives a grotesque message from Ramsay, and Yara chooses action over her father’s pride, sailing with a small force to attempt a rescue. At Dragonstone, Davos tries to save Gendry by smuggling him out, but is caught—only to stay alive because the letter from the Wall forces Stannis to confront a larger war than his claim to the throne. Melisandre burns the message and sees the coming conflict in the flames, redirecting Stannis northward. 
10

Across the Narrow Sea, Daenerys walks into the role she’s been chasing all season: not just conqueror, but liberator. The freed people of Yunkai surge toward her, chanting “mhysa”—“mother”—and lift her above the crowd as her dragons fly overhead. It’s a triumphant image, but also a warning: devotion can become a weapon, and liberation creates expectations that can crush the liberator if she can’t meet them. 
10
